title: Still Kicking — EN/DE/MI (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar German Maori language learning warm baritone 104bpm walking bass brushed drums trilingual resilience true story Australian family
lyrics:
[Verse 1 - English]
Coward punch. Neck surgery. Silver Chain.
"You alive?" "Still kicking."
He went to see a psychologist.
The kind of man who can do that is not beaten.

[Verse 2 - German, with English translations]
Feiger Schlag. Nackenchirurgie. Silver Chain jeden Morgen. (Coward punch. Neck surgery. Silver Chain every morning.)
"Lebst du noch?" "Noch am Kämpfen." (You alive? Still kicking.)
Er ging zu einem Psychologen. (He went to see a psychologist.)
Das sagte er in einer Textnachricht. (He said that in a text.)
An seinen Bruder. (To his brother.)
Ein Mann, der das tun kann (A man who can do that)
Wird von einem feigen Schlag nicht besiegt. (Is not beaten by a coward punch.)
Der Hals wird besser. (The neck is coming good.)

[Chorus - Māori, with English translations]
E tū tonu ana (Still kicking / still standing)
I whakautu ia i tērā i a rātou i ui ai (He answered that when they asked)
E tū tonu ana (Still kicking)
I waea mai a Corey mai i Parāsira (From Brazil, Corey called)
E tū tonu ana (Still kicking)
Ko Joel kei tērā taha o te waea (Joel on the other end of the line)
E tū tonu ana (Still kicking)
Ko ia tonu — ko Joel Aaron McIvor (That is him — Joel Aaron McIvor)

[Bridge - all three]
English: The family comes through. One thing at a time.
German: Die Familie kommt durch. Eine Sache nach der anderen. (The family comes through. One thing at a time.)
Māori: Ka taea e te whānau. Kotahi mea ia wā. (The family comes through. One thing at a time.)

[Outro - all three]
English: Still kicking — yes
German: Noch am Kämpfen — ja (Still kicking — yes)
Māori: E tū tonu ana — āe (Still kicking — yes)
